Amid progress on vaccinations and strong policy support, indicators of activity and employment had strengthened, and the FOMC reaffirmed an accommodative stance consistent with its average inflation targeting framework announced by Powell at Jackson Hole (2020). In the Clarida–Galí–Gertler view of forward‑looking policy rules, committing to hold rates at the zero lower bound and continue QE until “substantial further progress” is a dovish signal that should support demand via lower term premia and anchored expectations. The statement’s emphasis that inflation pressures were “largely transitory” and that longer‑term expectations remained well anchored aligns with inflation‑forecast‑focused guidance (Svensson and Woodford, 2005). Still, the explicit recognition that the outlook “depends on the course of the virus” reflects elevated pandemic‑related uncertainty, which tempers the tone. Netting these, the communication reads moderately positive.
